Making of the Computer Graphics for Star Wars (Episode IV)

That screen is not a graphics screen we are used to nowadays. It is a vector graphics, back in those times there was not enough RAM to store a complete image.

Vector graphics is basically an oscilloscope where you control the beam with X and Y voltages. So you can move the dot in X and Y coordinates but very fast. By having only the endpoints of each line stored you could give the appearance of a line.

The limitation of the number of lines is determined by the number of X and Y coordinates you could store. One of the interesting things of vector graphics is that the more endpoints you stored, the less bright the line became because it had to share the lines with other data points.

e.g. If I only have 2 endpoints, that line can be moved up and down 60 times a second. creating a very bright line. When I have 4 endpoints then that beam could only go 30 times between each points, reducing the brightness by halve.

Counter-Strike. A classic FPS that started off as a mod for Half Life ( the first game) that was later bought by Valve to make what is played today (Counter Strike: Global Offensive). The best way to get into CS is to just play whatever mode you like. For casual play you have Deathmatch, Gun Game, Casual mode and whatever custom servers you can find (I played far too much Surf RPG Deathmatch). If you want to play competitively, watch pros and watch vids/read guides about how to buy/what to buy and when, as well as looking up how to do specific smokes and mollies (molotovs).

I would point out that just about any game, competitive or not, can turn into trolling and namecalling, while I haven't faced that TOO much in CS I may have some bias as I've been playing that game for most of my life and think it's the quintessential FPS (maybe outside of DOOM or Wolfenstein)
